manufacturing_traditions.name: Human Commercial
manufacturing_traditions.philosophy: Build around standardized modules, broad supplier choice and field repair.
recognition: unused mounting points left for future equipment
manufacturing_traditions.failure_character: A Human ship may contain three generations of solutions to the same problem, all still connected.

manufacturing_traditions.name: Kesh Heavy
manufacturing_traditions.philosophy: Structure first, redundancy second, convenience after survival.
manufacturing_traditions.failure_character: Usually continues operating degraded; when something finally exceeds design margin, the event is rarely subtle.

manufacturing_traditions.name: Ilyan Efficient
manufacturing_traditions.failure_character: Excellent when maintained to specification; careless substitutions can cascade because margins were intentionally allocated rather than simply oversized.

manufacturing_traditions.name: Vey Closed-Cycle
manufacturing_traditions.philosophy: A ship is an artificial ecosystem whose outputs should become inputs.
manufacturing_traditions.failure_character: Environmental systems often degrade gracefully because flows can be rerouted, but contamination can spread through interconnected loops.

manufacturing_traditions.name: Orun Integrated
manufacturing_traditions.philosophy: Machinery should remain reachable from where people actually live and work.
recognition: machinery sharing walls with common spaces
manufacturing_traditions.failure_character: Easy to reach and patch; noise, heat or vibration may intrude into habitation long before a system actually fails.

common_hybrid_patterns.name: New Houston Independent
common_hybrid_patterns.description: Human-style modular hull, Ilyan propulsion, Vey environmental plant, Kesh structural components and whatever thermal equipment was affordable. Extremely common among owner-operators.

common_hybrid_patterns.name: Meridian Frontier Refit
common_hybrid_patterns.description: Existing ship modified for range and repairability: extra tanks, external racks, redundant comms, survey sensors, spare-part lockers and visibly non-original radiators.

common_hybrid_patterns.name: Carver Bulk Conversion
common_hybrid_patterns.description: Older hull stripped of passenger or specialty spaces and converted into ugly high-volume ore or container carrier. Cheap, slow and profitable on the right route.

shipboard_details: Manufacturer data plates are rarely decorative; experienced crews photograph them before buying used equipment.
External patch plates are not automatically signs of neglect. Properly documented repairs can remain certified for decades.
Commercial bridges favor physical emergency controls even when routine operation is computerized.
Large ships maintain lockers of adapters because interstellar standards reduce incompatibility rather than eliminating it.
Paint is often applied for corrosion/thermal reasons first and branding second.
Owner-operated ships accumulate nonstandard shelves, hooks, labels and storage wherever crews discover wasted space.
Exterior cargo changes a ship's silhouette from voyage to voyage.
